name: – Ingeborg Ter Laak – Commission proposal
title: REPORT on the proposal for a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council suspending the application of the rules on the appointment of authorised representatives for extended producer responsibility for waste, waste electrical and electronical equipment and single use plastic waste
part_text:
**What this report does**

The European Parliament's environment committee wants to pause one paperwork rule. Under current European Union rules, a company selling textiles, shoes, electrical goods or single-use plastic items in another European Union country must name an authorised representative there. The committee wants small and micro companies based in the European Union to be exempt from this until 1 January 2035, or until a new wider law on producer responsibility applies, whichever comes first. Bigger companies would still have to name a representative.

**Key points**

- Small and micro European Union producers no longer have to name an authorised representative in each country where they sell.
- Producers based outside the European Union keep the current rules; the exemption is only for European Union firms.
- The full Parliament will vote on this position; it is not yet law.
